description:
Look through binoculars from the South Korean side of the DMZ and you'll see a tidy little town with bright blue roofs, a school, a hospital and a water tower. But the windows have no glass, and nobody lives there.

This is the full history of North Korea, from a magazine map used to split a peninsula in thirty minutes in 1945 to a cryptocurrency heist worth $1.5 billion in 2025. In this video, we cover:

How two American colonels drew the 38th parallel
The Korean War and the armistice that never became peace
Kim Il Sung, Kim Jong Il and the myths built around them
The Arduous March famine of the 1990s
The prison camps and the killing of Kim Jong Nam
Nuclear weapons, sanctions and the balloon war
North Korean troops fighting for Russia in Ukraine
The Lazarus Group and the Bybit hack.

title: The ENTIRE History of United States of America in 16 Minutes
views_per_day_limitation: Snapshot views divided by age at retrieval; not a historical velocity series.
description:
Two hundred and fifty years ago, the United States didn't exist. No flag. No president. No army. Just thirteen small colonies on the edge of a continent, ruled by a king who never set foot on their soil.

This video takes you through the entire story — from the Native civilizations who lived here long before European contact, through colonization, revolution, and the Constitution, into westward expansion, slavery, and the Civil War, through industrialization, two World Wars, the Great Depression, the Cold War, the Civil Rights Movement, and into the modern era of 9/11, the financial crisis, and the digital age.

Every major turning point connects to the next. Every chapter creates the conditions for the one that follows. This isn't a list of dates — it's the story of how thirteen colonies became a superpower, and why some of the arguments from 1776 are still being fought today.

Chapters covered include: colonization and the thirteen colonies, the American Revolution, the Declaration of Independence and the Constitution, westward expansion and Manifest Destiny, the Civil War and Reconstruction, the Industrial Revolution and immigration, World War I and the Roaring Twenties, the Great Depression and the New Deal, World War II, the Cold War, the Civil Rights Movement, Vietnam and Watergate, and America in the 21st century.

If you're interested in American history, world history, or how the modern United States came to be, this documentary is for you.

This video covers difficult chapters in American history, including slavery, war, and displacement, in an honest and balanced way appropriate for a general audience.

description:
Most videos about Rome open with a wolf raising two abandoned twins and end with the same fall-of-empire story you've already heard a dozen times. This one is different. It's built around three discoveries about Rome that almost no other history video on this topic has ever mentioned — and one of them is only a few months old.

This documentary explores the complete history of the Roman Empire, from the founding of the Republic in 509 BC, the Punic Wars against Hannibal and Carthage, Julius Caesar's rise and assassination, and Augustus becoming Rome's first emperor, to the Pax Romana, the fall of the Western Empire in 476 AD, and the nearly thousand-year survival of the Byzantine Empire until 1453. Along the way, discover the 2023 MIT and Harvard study that finally explained why Roman concrete self-heals its own cracks, the 2025 skeletal discovery in York that provided the first physical proof gladiators really fought lions, and the still-unsolved mystery of the Roman dodecahedra — over 130 objects found, and not a single ancient text that explains what they were for.

This documentary is based on archaeological discoveries, historical sources, and academic research. We help bring history to life while remaining faithful to the historical record.

description:
For three hundred years, every king who fought the Vikings believed the same thing: beat them in battle, and they disappear. Instead, the exact same impossible pattern happened again and again — the Vikings lost the battle, and somehow still ended up wearing the crown.

This documentary explores the complete history of the Vikings, from the first raid on Lindisfarne in 793 and the Great Heathen Army, to Alfred the Great and the Danelaw, Rollo's conquest of Normandy and William the Conqueror's bloodline, Rurik and the founding of Kievan Rus, Cnut's North Sea Empire, and Leif Erikson's voyage to North America five hundred years before Columbus — proven down to the exact year by a 2021 tree-ring study. Discover how raiders who kept losing on the battlefield ended up founding the royal bloodlines of England, France, and Russia, and why the horned-helmet Viking you picture was invented centuries later by an opera costume designer.

title: The ENTIRE History of CHINA in 13 Minutes

description:
For over two thousand years, the same nightmare has repeated itself in China, again and again, like clockwork. A dynasty rises from chaos, grows wealthy and powerful, slowly rots from the inside, and collapses completely — only for China to rebuild itself, often larger and stronger than before. This has happened at least six times across four thousand years. And it might still be happening today.

This documentary explores the complete history of China's dynastic cycle, from the Mandate of Heaven and the Zhou dynasty's rise in 1046 BC, the terror and collapse of Qin Shi Huang's First Empire, the golden ages of the Han and Tang dynasties, the Mongol conquest under Kublai Khan and the rise of the Yuan dynasty, the Ming dynasty's treasure fleets, and the fall of the Qing dynasty in 1912, to the founding of the People's Republic of China in 1949, the Great Leap Forward, and China's modern rise as a global superpower. Discover the ancient political idea that predicted its own downfall three thousand years before anyone else, and why historians still debate whether China's current system will face the same fate as every dynasty before it.

This documentary is based on archaeological discoveries, historical sources, and academic research. We help bring history to life while remaining faithful to the historical record.

description:
World history has never seen an empire quite like the Ottomans. For 623 years, a dynasty that began as a small band of warriors on the edge of the Byzantine frontier grew into a superpower stretching across three continents, conquering an ancient capital, terrifying all of Europe, and outlasting almost every rival empire around it. And when it finally fell, it didn't just collapse — it was reborn as something entirely new.

This documentary explores the complete history of the Ottoman Empire, from Osman I and the empire's founding in 1299, Mehmed the Conqueror's fall of Constantinople in 1453, and the golden age of Suleiman the Magnificent, to the devshirme system, the 1683 Battle of Vienna, the long decline as "the sick man of Europe," the collapse during World War I, and the rise of the modern Republic of Turkey under Mustafa Kemal Atatürk. Discover how a small frontier tribe built one of history's longest-ruling dynasties, why an entire child-levy system powered its golden age, and how its fall gave birth to one of the most unique secular nations in the Muslim world.

This documentary is based on archaeological discoveries, historical sources, and academic research. We help bring history to life while remaining faithful to the historical record.
